ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 11, rod AB rotates about point A at a constant angular velocity, and drives the small ring of mass M fitted on the smooth horizontal rod OC to move. At the beginning of the motion, rod AB is in the vertical position. How does the velocity of the small ring M change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a vertical wall surface, and point A is below as the rotating hinge point of rod AB; directly above point A there is point O, and through point O to the right is a smooth horizontal rod OC. The small ring M is fitted on the horizontal rod OC, while rod AB passes through the small ring; in the figure, AB extends obliquely upward to the right from point A and intersects the horizontal rod near M. The vertical distance from A to O is labeled h, and rod AB rotates about point A at a constant angular velocity ω. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, at the beginning of the motion rod AB is in the vertical position. Let the angle through which rod AB has turned from the initial vertical position be θ; then because the angular velocity is constant, θ=ωt. The small ring M can only move along the horizontal rod OC, and its position is the intersection point of rod AB and the horizontal rod OC. The vertical distance from A to the horizontal rod is h, so when the angle between the rod and the vertical direction is θ, the horizontal displacement of the small ring relative to point O is x=h tanθ. Differentiate with respect to time: v_M=dx/dt=h·sec^2θ·dθ/dt=hω sec^2θ. At the beginning θ=0; afterward θ gradually increases, and sec^2θ increases as θ increases, so the velocity of the small ring M gradually increases.
